History invariance, ordinary-coalition compression, tied-top order use, exactly-two selective restoration, temperature, lapse, and all other equations and parameter ranges are preserved.

experiment.rationale: This design exploits a qualitative disagreement about an inactive co-top-validity expert. Experts 4 and 6 are tied at 90%, but Expert 4 is presented earlier. Expert 4 always favors the designated anchor option. In each off/on matched pair, the active evidence changes only by Expert 6: in the off condition Expert 6 is nondiscriminating, whereas in the on condition Expert 6 favors the opposing option. The remaining evidence is three-versus-three when Expert 6 is off and three-versus-four when it is on; Expert 1 always belongs to the opposing coalition, so ADCG's minority-first profile gate is not activated. PDRR treats the off condition as having a unique active anchor and therefore supplies no order gate. Because its ordinary validity compression makes the equal-sized coalitions nearly exchangeable, it predicts only a small Expert-4 advantage. Activating Expert 6 creates an exact active top-validity tie, causing PDRR's bounded order gate to favor the earlier Expert 4 despite adding strong evidence to the opposing coalition. PDRR therefore predicts a positive change in anchor-option choice from off to on. ADCG instead computes its global-top-tie gate from the full instructed validity profile, including nondiscriminating experts. Its tie gate is consequently already present in the off condition and does not newly appear when Expert 6 becomes active. Adding the equally valid Expert 6 to the opposition should reduce anchor choices; repeated perfect opposition between Experts 6 and 4 can further amplify this reduction through learned anti-concurrence. Thus the critical quantitative statistic is P(anchor option | Expert 6 on) minus P(anchor option | Expert 6 off): PDRR predicts a positive contrast, whereas ADCG predicts a negative contrast, potentially becoming more negative with experience. Three lower-cue allocations test generality across serial composition, and exact A/B reversals control response-side preferences. The 12 unique pairs are repeated eight times for 96 trials.

metric.rationale: This is the preregistered activation contrast P(anchor option | Expert 6 discriminates) minus P(anchor option | Expert 6 is nondiscriminating). It uses all 96 trials and expresses responses relative to the option supported by Expert 4, so the exact A/B reversals cancel response-side preferences. PDRR predicts a positive value because activating the tied 90%-valid Expert 6 introduces its bounded order gate favoring the earlier Expert 4. ADCG predicts a negative value because its global tied-top gate is already present when Expert 6 is inactive, while activation adds strong opposition to Expert 4 and can acquire further anti-concurrence weight over the block. The within-subject difference also removes much stable variation in overall anchor preference and lapse rate, improving precision at the small human sample size.

proposer_theory.description: Adaptive Distinctive Coalition Gating (ADCG) proposes that binary-feature decisions arise from task-adaptive cue weights combining communicated validity, presentation prominence, distributional rarity, and learned cue dependence. Directionally concordant cues are compressed as potentially redundant, while sparse dissent can dominate when its cues have reliably and repeatedly opposed the anchor's cues. Learned anti-concurrence is reliability-sensitive: disagreement near chance is strongly suppressed, whereas well-observed disagreement above a subject-specific threshold receives a bounded nonlinear gain. A profile-driven gate interpolates between coalition comparison and a lexicographic anchor, preserving anchoring against large redundant coalitions while permitting diagnostic opposition to suppress it. For compact opposition, gate suppression is controlled by a selective summary of the strongest reliably learned opposing relationship rather than an indiscriminate average across all cue pairs; larger coalitions retain mean aggregation and strong size decay. In addition, a unique, early-presented validity anchor loses accessibility within the coalition core when it faces compact, reliably anti-concurrent opposition. This attenuation targets residual anchoring without increasing dissent support and vanishes for tied-validity anchors, late anchors, and large opposing coalitions. When top validities are tied, presentation order supplies a bounded anchor but the distinctive-coalition core is attenuated by a stable subject-specific amount. Stable variation in validity attention, order prominence, anti-concurrence threshold and gain, diagnostic selectivity, anchor attenuation, tied-top attenuation, redundancy, gating, and temperature produces structured individual differences without experiment-specific strategies.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"ADCG expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )

    n_features = stim.shape[1]
    validities = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if validities.ndim != 1 or validities.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {validities.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    # Positive directions favor B; negative directions favor A.
    directions = np.sign(stim[1] - stim[0])
    active = np.flatnonzero(directions != 0)
    if active.size == 0:
        return np.array([0.5, 0.5], dtype=np.float64)

    validity_attention = float(parameters["validity_attention"])
    order_prominence = float(parameters["order_prominence"])
    distribution_attention = float(parameters["distribution_attention"])
    distinctiveness = float(parameters["distinctiveness"])
    dissent_bonus = float(parameters["dissent_bonus"])
    anti_concurrence_attention = float(parameters["anti_concurrence_attention"])
    anti_concurrence_threshold = float(parameters["anti_concurrence_threshold"])
    diagnostic_selectivity = float(parameters["diagnostic_selectivity"])
    anchor_attenuation = float(parameters["anchor_attenuation"])
    redundancy = float(parameters["redundancy"])
    lex_strength = float(parameters["lex_strength"])
    gate_sharpness = float(parameters["gate_sharpness"])
    gate_rarity = float(parameters["gate_rarity"])
    tie_gate_ceiling = float(parameters["tie_gate_ceiling"])
    tie_core_attenuation = float(parameters["tie_core_attenuation"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])

    # Communicated validity is represented on a reliability-evidence scale.
    v = np.clip(validities, 0.500001, 0.999999)
    reliability = np.log(v / (1.0 - v))
    reliability = (reliability - np.mean(reliability)) / (
        np.std(reliability) + 0.35
    )

    # Estimate how often each cue discriminates and how often cue pairs
    # concur. Symmetric pseudocounts make the model well-defined early in
    # the block while allowing randomized task experience to update weights.
    past_a = history.get("option_a_ratings", [])
    past_b = history.get("option_b_ratings", [])
    n_past = min(len(past_a), len(past_b))

    discr_count = np.ones(n_features, dtype=float) * 2.0
    pair_both = np.ones((n_features, n_features), dtype=float) * 2.0
    pair_same = np.ones((n_features, n_features), dtype=float)

    for i in range(n_past):
        pa = np.asarray(past_a[i], dtype=float)
        pb = np.asarray(past_b[i], dtype=float)
        if pa.shape[0] != n_features or pb.shape[0] != n_features:
            continue
        s = np.sign(pb - pa)
        on = np.flatnonzero(s != 0)
        discr_count[on] += 1.0
        for q, j in enumerate(on):
            for k in on[q + 1:]:
                pair_both[j, k] += 1.0
                pair_both[k, j] += 1.0
                if s[j] == s[k]:
                    pair_same[j, k] += 1.0
                    pair_same[k, j] += 1.0

    discr_rate = discr_count / float(n_past + 4.0)
    reference_rate = float(np.mean(discr_rate))
    rarity = np.clip(reference_rate / discr_rate, 0.35, 3.5)

    # Learned anti-concurrence is high only for cue pairs that repeatedly
    # discriminate in opposite directions. Pair-specific observation counts
    # determine reliability, and a steep subject-specific threshold removes
    # weak or chance-level disagreement while retaining systematic dissent.
    anti_concurrence = np.clip(1.0 - pair_same / pair_both, 0.0, 1.0)
    pair_observations = np.maximum(pair_both - 2.0, 0.0)
    pair_confidence = pair_observations / (pair_observations + 2.0)
    pair_confidence *= np.clip((pair_observations - 1.0) / 3.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    threshold_baseline = 1.0 / (
        1.0 + np.exp(-18.0 * (0.5 - anti_concurrence_threshold))
    )
    thresholded_anti = 1.0 / (
        1.0 + np.exp(-18.0 * (anti_concurrence - anti_concurrence_threshold))
    )
    thresholded_anti = np.clip(
        (thresholded_anti - threshold_baseline)
        / max(1.0 - threshold_baseline, 1e-12),
        0.0,
        1.0,
    )
    learned_anti = pair_confidence * thresholded_anti

    # Baseline cue accessibility combines instructed validity, serial
    # prominence, and learned distributional rarity.
    if n_features > 1:
        position = 1.0 - np.arange(n_features, dtype=float) / (n_features - 1.0)
    else:
        position = np.ones(1, dtype=float)
    cue_weight = np.exp(
        validity_attention * reliability
        + order_prominence * position
        + distribution_attention * np.log(rarity)
    )

    # Cues that historically concur with their current coalition partners
    # are treated as less independent. A cue with no partner is not given
    # this historical redundancy penalty.
    for j in active:
        partners = [
            int(k) for k in active
            if k != j and directions[k] == directions[j]
        ]
        if partners:
            concurrence = [pair_same[j, k] / pair_both[j, k] for k in partners]
            corr_load = float(np.mean(concurrence))
            cue_weight[j] /= 1.0 + redundancy * corr_load

    a_cues = np.flatnonzero(directions < 0)
    b_cues = np.flatnonzero(directions > 0)
    n_a = int(a_cues.size)
    n_b = int(b_cues.size)

    # Lexicographic anchor: highest communicated validity among currently
    # discriminating cues, with stable presentation order breaking ties.
    active_validity = validities[active]
    best_validity = float(np.max(active_validity))
    best_candidates = active[np.isclose(active_validity, best_validity, atol=1e-10)]
    lex_cue = int(np.min(best_candidates))
    lex_direction = float(directions[lex_cue])

    # A global top-validity tie attenuates profile-based singleton
    # amplification, preventing the first cue from receiving both a strong
    # order anchor and a full distinctiveness bonus.
    sorted_v = np.sort(validities)[::-1]
    if sorted_v.size >= 2:
        top_gap = float(sorted_v[0] - sorted_v[1])
        global_top_tie = float(np.exp(-80.0 * top_gap))
    else:
        global_top_tie = 1.0
    tie_core_multiplier = 1.0 - tie_core_attenuation * global_top_tie

    # Current-profile distinctiveness: members of the smaller directional
    # coalition stand out, while each coalition's accumulated contribution
    # is divided by a redundancy term.
    if n_a > 0 and n_b > 0:
        if n_a < n_b:
            cue_weight[a_cues] *= (float(n_b) / float(n_a)) ** (
                distinctiveness * tie_core_multiplier
            )
        elif n_b < n_a:
            cue_weight[b_cues] *= (float(n_a) / float(n_b)) ** (
                distinctiveness * tie_core_multiplier
            )

        # Sparse evidence opposing the validity-defined anchor receives its
        # ordinary bounded bonus. Additional influence is restricted to
        # dissenting cues with reliably learned above-threshold opposition.
        dissent_cues = a_cues if lex_direction > 0 else b_cues
        anchor_cues = b_cues if lex_direction > 0 else a_cues
        n_dissent = int(dissent_cues.size)
        if n_dissent > 0:
            for j in dissent_cues:
                learned_diagnosticity = 0.0
                if anchor_cues.size > 0:
                    learned_diagnosticity = float(
                        np.mean(learned_anti[j, anchor_cues])
                    )
                bonus = 1.0 + (dissent_bonus / float(n_dissent)) * (
                    1.0
                    + anti_concurrence_attention * learned_diagnosticity
                )
                cue_weight[j] *= bonus

            # A unique and presentation-prominent validity anchor becomes
            # less accessible in the coalition core when compact opposition
            # has a reliably learned anti-concurrent relationship with it.
            # Active-cue validity uniqueness leaves tied-top profiles intact;
            # squared prominence and size decay protect late anchors and
            # anchors facing large, plausibly redundant coalitions.
            if active_validity.size >= 2:
                sorted_active_v = np.sort(active_validity)[::-1]
                active_gap = float(sorted_active_v[0] - sorted_active_v[1])
                anchor_uniqueness = 1.0 - np.exp(-80.0 * active_gap)
            else:
                anchor_uniqueness = 1.0
            anchor_diagnosticity = float(
                np.max(learned_anti[dissent_cues, lex_cue])
            )
            compact_decay = np.exp(-1.5 * float(n_dissent - 1))
            anchor_signal = (
                anchor_uniqueness
                * float(position[lex_cue] ** 2)
                * anchor_diagnosticity
                * compact_decay
            )
            cue_weight[lex_cue] *= np.exp(
                -anchor_attenuation * anchor_signal
            )

    support_a = 0.0
    support_b = 0.0
    if n_a > 0:
        support_a = float(np.sum(cue_weight[a_cues])) / (float(n_a) ** redundancy)
    if n_b > 0:
        support_b = float(np.sum(cue_weight[b_cues])) / (float(n_b) ** redundancy)

    scale = support_a + support_b
    core_evidence = (support_b - support_a) / max(scale, 1e-12)

    # A near tie among the two globally strongest instructed validities
    # raises the stable-order gate, but anchoring has a subject-specific
    # ceiling rather than becoming obligatorily lexicographic.
    tied_top_gate = tie_gate_ceiling * global_top_tie

    # Profile-driven anchoring occurs when the earliest discriminating cue
    # is on an isolated minority side. It is attenuated when a sparse cue in
    # the opposing coalition is historically rare or reliably
    # anti-concurrent, while a large opposition remains interpretable as
    # redundant evidence.
    first_cue = int(active[0])
    first_side_count = n_b if directions[first_cue] > 0 else n_a
    other_side_count = n_a if directions[first_cue] > 0 else n_b
    if first_side_count > 0 and other_side_count > 0:
        isolation = 1.0 - float(first_side_count) / float(other_side_count)
        minority_first = float(first_side_count < other_side_count)
        opposing_cues = a_cues if directions[first_cue] > 0 else b_cues
        first_side_cues = b_cues if directions[first_cue] > 0 else a_cues
        opposing_rarity = float(np.max(np.maximum(np.log(rarity[opposing_cues]), 0.0)))
        opposing_distinctiveness = opposing_rarity / (
            np.log(3.5) * np.sqrt(float(other_side_count))
        )

        # For compact opposition, a reliability-weighted soft maximum lets
        # one strongly diagnostic relation disengage the anchor without
        # being diluted by weak pairings. Larger coalitions retain mean
        # aggregation, and all configurations retain exponential size decay.
        opposition_relations = learned_anti[
            np.ix_(opposing_cues, first_side_cues)
        ].reshape(-1)
        if other_side_count <= 3 and opposition_relations.size > 1:
            select_logits = diagnostic_selectivity * (
                opposition_relations - np.max(opposition_relations)
            )
            select_weights = np.exp(select_logits)
            select_weights /= np.sum(select_weights)
            learned_opposition = float(
                np.sum(select_weights * opposition_relations)
            )
        else:
            learned_opposition = float(np.mean(opposition_relations))
        learned_opposition *= np.exp(-1.5 * float(other_side_count - 1))
        opposing_distinctiveness += (
            anti_concurrence_attention * learned_opposition
        )
    else:
        isolation = 0.0
        minority_first = 0.0
        opposing_distinctiveness = 0.0

    profile_gate = minority_first / (
        1.0 + np.exp(-gate_sharpness * (isolation - 0.30))
    )
    profile_gate *= np.exp(-gate_rarity * opposing_distinctiveness)
    gate = 1.0 - (1.0 - tied_top_gate) * (1.0 - profile_gate)
    gate = float(np.clip(gate, 0.0, 1.0))

    choice_evidence = (
        (1.0 - gate) * core_evidence
        + gate * lex_strength * lex_direction
    )

    logits = beta * np.array([-0.5 * choice_evidence, 0.5 * choice_evidence])
    logits = logits - np.max(logits)
    probs = np.exp(logits)
    probs /= probs.sum()
    return probs.astype(np.float64)
proposer_theory.rationale: This is a two-range calibration of the accepted iteration-9 ADCG source; no equations or pathways are added. First, the upper bound of anchor_attenuation increases from 2.4 to 3.2 while its lower bound remains fixed. Because attenuation is already conditional on a unique validity anchor, early presentation, high-confidence anti-concurrence, and compact opposition, the added strength and subject heterogeneity are localized to the residual failures in Experiments 2 and 6. Tied-top profiles, late anchors, and large opposing coalitions remain protected by the existing multiplicative exclusions and size decay. Second, redundancy shifts modestly from [0.75, 1.25] to [0.68, 1.15]. This slightly softens generic coalition compression, reducing the excessive balanced-versus-imbalanced effect in Experiment 3. It should also modestly reduce excess top-cue adherence in Experiments 2 and 5 and strengthen the negative multi-opponent contrast in Experiment 6, while the unchanged large-coalition profile gate preserves Experiment 1. The successful gate-only soft maximum, mean direct diagnostic bonus, tied-top mechanisms, and all confidence computations are otherwise retained exactly.

next_theory.description: Active-Cue Accessibility Competition (ACAC) proposes that people use a stable representation of communicated cue validity and evaluate only cues that discriminate on the current trial. Active cues first form option-specific coalitions. Coalition support accumulates smoothly but is compressed according to coalition size, validity similarity, and effective cue multiplicity, so additional concordant cues become increasingly redundant without triggering a categorical restoration rule. In unique-anchor configurations where both options have multiple active supporters, coalition evidence is additionally normalized toward effective coalition counts. This prevents the allocation of one relatively valid lower cue from producing an implicit presentation-order crossover. Decisions in this symmetrically normalized geometry are made with moderately greater response precision, reflecting reduced conflict after cue identities have been compressed; this suppresses sampling-induced primacy classifications and strengthens balanced-profile anchor evidence without introducing an order weight. The strongest currently active cue serves as a validity anchor. Opposition receives a sharply count-selective challenge enhancement centered on exactly one opponent. This enhancement is strongest for an isolated anchor and attenuated for embedded-anchor singleton dissent; larger opposing coalitions retain only a small, smooth inverse-count challenge tail. In the exact unique-anchor, isolated, one-opponent configuration, stable competition types form a heterogeneous mixture containing a small genuinely resistant group and a larger set of strongly challenge-accessible integrators. Challenge strength depends continuously on the anchor's absolute validity and validity advantage over the strongest opponent. Presentation order is consulted only when multiple currently active cues share maximal communicated validity. A bounded active-tie gate favors the earliest member of that tied set, with an additional conflict-geometry increment when lower-validity active cues precede tied maxima supporting opposing options. Inactive co-top cues cannot activate either component. Tie accessibility retains the same marginal distribution across subject types as in the previous model. Because the task provides no correctness feedback, ACAC explicitly excludes trial-history learning of cue concurrence, anti-concurrence, or discrimination frequency.
next_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"ACAC expects state with shape (2, n_features); got {stim.shape}."
        )

    n_features = stim.shape[1]
    validities = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if validities.ndim != 1 or validities.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {validities.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    # Positive directions favor B and negative directions favor A.
    directions = np.sign(stim[1] - stim[0])
    active = np.flatnonzero(directions != 0)
    if active.size == 0:
        return np.array([0.5, 0.5], dtype=np.float64)

    validity_gain = float(parameters["validity_gain"])
    redundancy_strength = float(parameters["redundancy_strength"])
    redundancy_curvature = float(parameters["redundancy_curvature"])
    similarity_sensitivity = float(parameters["similarity_sensitivity"])
    compact_challenge = float(parameters["compact_challenge"])
    compact_peak = float(parameters["compact_peak"])
    compact_width = float(parameters["compact_width"])
    isolated_singleton_access = float(parameters["isolated_singleton_access"])
    challenge_tail = float(parameters["challenge_tail"])
    embedded_compact_scale = float(parameters["embedded_compact_scale"])
    challenge_gap_scale = float(parameters["challenge_gap_scale"])
    absolute_threshold = float(parameters["absolute_threshold"])
    absolute_slope = float(parameters["absolute_slope"])
    weak_anchor_gain = float(parameters["weak_anchor_gain"])
    isolation_gain = float(parameters["isolation_gain"])
    credibility_protection = float(parameters["credibility_protection"])
    active_tie_ceiling = float(parameters["active_tie_ceiling"])
    tie_activation_rate = float(parameters["tie_activation_rate"])
    conflict_tie_boost = float(parameters["conflict_tie_boost"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    lapse = float(parameters["lapse"])
    competition_type = int(parameters["competition_type"])

    # Six correlated mixture cells preserve the previous marginal distribution
    # of active-tie accessibility while assigning only one-sixth of subjects to
    # a genuinely singleton-resistant group. The remaining subjects express a
    # strong but heterogeneous exact-singleton challenge response.
    if competition_type == 0:       # genuinely singleton-resistant
        type_challenge = 0.05
        type_singleton_access = 0.00
    elif competition_type in (1, 2):  # strongly challenge-sensitive
        type_challenge = 4.50
        type_singleton_access = 0.00
    else:                            # strongly accessible integrators
        type_challenge = 1.00
        type_singleton_access = 1.50

    # Tie accessibility is crossed with singleton sensitivity so that changing
    # the singleton mixture does not change the marginal tie-type frequencies.
    if competition_type in (0, 1):
        type_tie = 1.65
    elif competition_type in (2, 3):
        type_tie = 0.30
    else:
        type_tie = 1.00

    def sigmoid(x):
        x = float(np.clip(x, -60.0, 60.0))
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-x))

    # Communicated accuracy is represented on a log-evidence scale. Centering
    # on the active maximum improves numerical stability without discarding
    # absolute validity, which is retained separately below.
    v = np.clip(validities, 0.500001, 0.999999)
    reliability = np.log(v / (1.0 - v))
    active_reference = float(np.max(reliability[active]))
    cue_weight = np.exp(validity_gain * (reliability - active_reference))

    a_cues = np.flatnonzero(directions < 0)
    b_cues = np.flatnonzero(directions > 0)
    n_a = int(a_cues.size)
    n_b = int(b_cues.size)

    def coalition_support(indices):
        n = int(indices.size)
        if n == 0:
            return 0.0

        weights = np.asarray(cue_weight[indices], dtype=float)
        raw_support = float(np.sum(weights))

        # Effective multiplicity changes smoothly with coalition composition.
        # A coalition containing several similarly accessible cues has a high
        # effective count and is compressed more strongly than a heterogeneous
        # coalition dominated by one cue.
        effective_n = raw_support / max(float(np.max(weights)), 1e-12)
        effective_excess = max(effective_n - 1.0, 0.0)

        coalition_v = validities[indices]
        validity_spread = float(np.std(coalition_v)) if n > 1 else 0.0
        similarity = np.exp(-similarity_sensitivity * validity_spread)
        discount = 1.0 + redundancy_strength * similarity * (
            effective_excess ** redundancy_curvature
        )
        return raw_support / max(discount, 1e-12)

    support_a = coalition_support(a_cues)
    support_b = coalition_support(b_cues)

    # The validity anchor is defined only over currently discriminating cues.
    active_v = validities[active]
    best_v = float(np.max(active_v))
    top_candidates = active[np.isclose(active_v, best_v, atol=1e-8)]
    anchor_cue = int(np.min(top_candidates))
    anchor_direction = float(directions[anchor_cue])
    unique_anchor = float(top_candidates.size == 1)

    # In unique-anchor multi-cue-versus-multi-cue configurations, normalize
    # coalition composition toward effective count support. This saturation
    # prevents reallocating one relatively valid lower cue from inducing an
    # implicit primacy crossover, while leaving isolated-anchor diagnostics
    # and all tied-top configurations unchanged.
    normalized_multicue_geometry = False
    if unique_anchor > 0.0 and n_a > 1 and n_b > 1:
        pooled_weight = float(np.mean(cue_weight[active]))

        def normalized_multicue_support(n):
            excess = float(n - 1)
            discount = 1.0 + redundancy_strength * (
                excess ** redundancy_curvature
            )
            return pooled_weight * float(n) / max(discount, 1e-12)

        support_a = normalized_multicue_support(n_a)
        support_b = normalized_multicue_support(n_b)
        normalized_multicue_geometry = True

    if anchor_direction > 0:
        anchor_indices = b_cues
        opponent_indices = a_cues
        anchor_support = support_b
        opponent_support = support_a
    else:
        anchor_indices = a_cues
        opponent_indices = b_cues
        anchor_support = support_a
        opponent_support = support_b

    anchor_count = int(anchor_indices.size)
    opponent_count = int(opponent_indices.size)

    # Absolute credibility and relative advantage are distinct. A cue can be
    # locally strongest yet remain challengeable when all active cues have low
    # communicated validity.
    weak_anchor = sigmoid(absolute_slope * (absolute_threshold - best_v))
    strong_anchor = 1.0 - weak_anchor

    if opponent_count > 0:
        strongest_opponent_v = float(np.max(validities[opponent_indices]))
        opponent_gap = max(best_v - strongest_opponent_v, 0.0)
    else:
        opponent_gap = 0.5

    gap_accessibility = np.exp(
        -opponent_gap / max(challenge_gap_scale, 1e-8)
    )
    gap_protection = 1.0 - gap_accessibility

    # Credibility protection is deliberately bounded so that merely moving a
    # relatively valid lower cue between coalitions cannot create an implicit
    # unique-anchor presentation-order effect.
    anchor_support *= 1.0 + (
        unique_anchor
        * credibility_protection
        * strong_anchor
        * gap_protection
    )

    if opponent_count > 0:
        # The high-amplitude component is extremely localized at one opponent.
        # Embedded singleton dissent receives only a bounded fraction of it,
        # whereas isolated one-versus-one conflict expresses the full stable
        # subject-type difference. In that exact geometry, a bounded access
        # increment selectively raises strongly accessible integrators while a
        # small mixture remains genuinely resistant.
        count_distance = (
            float(opponent_count) - compact_peak
        ) / max(compact_width, 1e-8)
        singleton_profile = np.exp(-0.5 * count_distance ** 2)

        if anchor_count == 1:
            singleton_geometry = 1.0
        else:
            singleton_geometry = embedded_compact_scale

        active_type_challenge = type_challenge
        if (
            unique_anchor > 0.0
            and anchor_count == 1
            and opponent_count == 1
            and top_candidates.size == 1
        ):
            active_type_challenge += (
                isolated_singleton_access * type_singleton_access
            )

        singleton_intensity = (
            active_type_challenge
            * compact_challenge
            * singleton_profile
            * singleton_geometry
        )
        smooth_tail = challenge_tail / float(opponent_count + 1)

        isolation = 1.0 / float(max(anchor_count, 1))
        geometry_gain = 1.0 + isolation_gain * isolation
        absolute_gain = 1.0 + weak_anchor_gain * weak_anchor

        challenge_multiplier = 1.0 + (
            singleton_intensity + smooth_tail
        ) * gap_accessibility * geometry_gain * absolute_gain
        opponent_support *= challenge_multiplier

    total_support = anchor_support + opponent_support
    if total_support <= 1e-12:
        core_evidence = 0.0
    else:
        anchor_margin = (anchor_support - opponent_support) / total_support
        core_evidence = anchor_direction * anchor_margin

    # A bounded order gate is activated exclusively by a tie among currently
    # active maximum-validity cues. Conflict among tied maxima receives an
    # additional activation increment only when lower-validity active cues
    # precede the tied set. This captures activation-sensitive accessibility
    # without increasing first-cue adherence in unique-maximum profiles.
    active_top_count = int(top_candidates.size)
    if active_top_count >= 2:
        tie_gate = (
            type_tie
            * active_tie_ceiling
            * (1.0 - np.exp(
                -tie_activation_rate * float(active_top_count - 1)
            ))
        )
        tied_directions = directions[top_candidates]
        tied_conflict = float(
            np.any(tied_directions > 0) and np.any(tied_directions < 0)
        )
        preceded_tied_set = float(int(active[0]) < anchor_cue)
        tie_gate += (
            type_tie
            * conflict_tie_boost
            * tied_conflict
            * preceded_tied_set
        )
    else:
        tie_gate = 0.0
    tie_gate = float(np.clip(tie_gate, 0.0, 0.95))

    choice_evidence = (
        (1.0 - tie_gate) * core_evidence
        + tie_gate * anchor_direction
    )

    # Symmetric multi-cue normalization removes much of the identity-based
    # conflict, so choices in that geometry are moderately more precise. This
    # affects neither isolated singleton competition nor active-top-tie trials.
    effective_beta = beta * (1.60 if normalized_multicue_geometry else 1.0)
    logits = effective_beta * np.array(
        [-0.5 * choice_evidence, 0.5 * choice_evidence],
        dtype=np.float64,
    )
    logits = logits - np.max(logits)
    probs = np.exp(logits)
    probs /= probs.sum()

    probs = (1.0 - lapse) * probs + lapse * np.array(
        [0.5, 0.5], dtype=np.float64
    )
    probs = np.clip(probs, 0.0, None)
    total = float(probs.sum())
    if not np.isfinite(total) or total <= 0.0:
        return np.array([0.5, 0.5], dtype=np.float64)
    probs /= total
    return probs.astype(np.float64)

First, it replaces the increasingly homogeneous three-type singleton loading with six equally sampled correlated mixture cells. Only one-sixth of subjects remains genuinely resistant in the exact unique-anchor, isolated one-opponent branch, while the other five-sixths receive strong challenge through either a larger baseline sensitivity or integrative accessibility. This should further lower Experiment-2 anchor adherence and deepen Experiment 6 while restoring the missing between-subject variance. Second, the existing hard symmetric normalization is left intact, but response precision is multiplied by 1.6 only in unique-anchor multi-cue-versus-multi-cue configurations. Experiment 4 has identical normalized coalition counts across its Expert-1 support conditions, so this reduces threshold-classification false positives without creating a conditional order effect. experiment.rationale: This design targets ACAC's special symmetric normalization for unique-anchor, multi-cue-versus-multi-cue profiles. Expert 6 is the unique 95% validity anchor and always supports the designated anchor option. Expert 1 (85%) always supports the opposing option and is therefore the strongest opponent in every trial. The critical manipulation swaps Expert 3 (82%) and Expert 4 (56%) between the two coalitions while holding the active cue set, coalition counts, anchor identity, strongest-opponent identity, and anchor-to-opponent validity gap constant. In the high-partner condition, the anchor coalition contains Experts 6 and 3, opposed by Experts 1 and 4. In the weak-partner condition, it contains Experts 6 and 4, opposed by Experts 1 and 3. Both configurations are exactly two-versus-two. ACAC consequently replaces both coalitions' supports with the same count-normalized quantities; its credibility protection and challenge terms are also identical because the 95% anchor and 85% strongest opponent are unchanged. ACAC therefore predicts an exactly zero contrast in probability of choosing the anchor option between the high-partner and weak-partner conditions, notwithstanding its potentially nonzero overall anchor preference. ADCG preserves cue-specific validity and serial weights. Expert 3 is both much more valid and earlier than Expert 4, so assigning Expert 3 to the anchor coalition simultaneously strengthens that coalition and removes a strong cue from the dissent coalition. Conversely, assigning Expert 3 to the opposition gives this already stronger cue ADCG's dissent amplification. ADCG therefore predicts substantially more anchor choices in the high-partner than in the weak-partner condition, potentially producing a choice crossover. Historical discrimination frequency is matched because Experts 1, 3, 4, and 6 discriminate on every trial. The schedule also symmetrically balances concurrence relationships involving Experts 3 and 4, while Expert 1's diagnostic opposition to the anchor is common to both conditions. Experts 2 and 5 are nondiscriminating fillers whose shared values generate three perceptually distinct versions of each profile without changing either theory's directional evidence. Exact A/B reversals control response-side preferences. The critical statistic is P(anchor choice | Expert 3 partners with anchor) minus P(anchor choice | Expert 4 partners with anchor): ACAC predicts exactly zero, whereas ADCG predicts a positive contrast. The 12 unique pairs are repeated eight times for 96 trials.

metric.rationale: This metric measures the overall probability of choosing the option supported by the unique 95%-validity anchor, pooling all 96 trials rather than differencing the two partner conditions. The failed conditional contrast discarded a potentially larger between-theory level difference and compounded sampling error from two separate rates. Under ACAC, every trial receives symmetric two-versus-two normalization; only its bounded credibility-protection and challenge-tail terms can shift choices away from approximate anchor indifference. Under ADCG, the two cues opposing the anchor receive an ordinary dissent bonus from the outset and an increasingly strong learned anti-concurrence bonus, especially because Expert 1 consistently opposes Expert 6. The profile gate does not restore lexicographic anchoring here because the earliest cue's coalition is not a numerical minority. ADCG should therefore produce substantially fewer anchor choices overall. Coding choices relative to Expert 6 combines A/B reversals, and using every trial yields a tight per-subject estimate.

proposer_theory.description: Active-Cue Accessibility Competition (ACAC) proposes that people use a stable representation of communicated cue validity and evaluate only cues that discriminate on the current trial. Active cues first form option-specific coalitions. Coalition support accumulates smoothly but is compressed according to coalition size, validity similarity, and effective cue multiplicity, so additional concordant cues become increasingly redundant without triggering a categorical restoration rule. In unique-anchor configurations where both options have multiple active supporters, coalition evidence is additionally normalized toward effective coalition counts. This prevents the allocation of one relatively valid lower cue from producing an implicit presentation-order crossover. Decisions in this symmetrically normalized geometry are made with moderately greater response precision, reflecting reduced conflict after cue identities have been compressed; this suppresses sampling-induced primacy classifications and strengthens balanced-profile anchor evidence without introducing an order weight. The strongest currently active cue serves as a validity anchor. Opposition receives a sharply count-selective challenge enhancement centered on exactly one opponent. This enhancement is strongest for an isolated anchor and attenuated for embedded-anchor singleton dissent; larger opposing coalitions retain only a small, smooth inverse-count challenge tail. In the exact unique-anchor, isolated, one-opponent configuration, stable competition types form a heterogeneous mixture containing a small genuinely resistant group and a larger set of strongly challenge-accessible integrators. Challenge strength depends continuously on the anchor's absolute validity and validity advantage over the strongest opponent. Presentation order is consulted only when multiple currently active cues share maximal communicated validity. A bounded active-tie gate favors the earliest member of that tied set, with an additional conflict-geometry increment when lower-validity active cues precede tied maxima supporting opposing options. Inactive co-top cues cannot activate either component. Tie accessibility retains the same marginal distribution across subject types as in the previous model. Because the task provides no correctness feedback, ACAC explicitly excludes trial-history learning of cue concurrence, anti-concurrence, or discrimination frequency.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"ACAC expects state with shape (2, n_features); got {stim.shape}."
        )

    n_features = stim.shape[1]
    validities = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if validities.ndim != 1 or validities.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {validities.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    # Positive directions favor B and negative directions favor A.
    directions = np.sign(stim[1] - stim[0])
    active = np.flatnonzero(directions != 0)
    if active.size == 0:
        return np.array([0.5, 0.5], dtype=np.float64)

    validity_gain = float(parameters["validity_gain"])
    redundancy_strength = float(parameters["redundancy_strength"])
    redundancy_curvature = float(parameters["redundancy_curvature"])
    similarity_sensitivity = float(parameters["similarity_sensitivity"])
    compact_challenge = float(parameters["compact_challenge"])
    compact_peak = float(parameters["compact_peak"])
    compact_width = float(parameters["compact_width"])
    isolated_singleton_access = float(parameters["isolated_singleton_access"])
    challenge_tail = float(parameters["challenge_tail"])
    embedded_compact_scale = float(parameters["embedded_compact_scale"])
    challenge_gap_scale = float(parameters["challenge_gap_scale"])
    absolute_threshold = float(parameters["absolute_threshold"])
    absolute_slope = float(parameters["absolute_slope"])
    weak_anchor_gain = float(parameters["weak_anchor_gain"])
    isolation_gain = float(parameters["isolation_gain"])
    credibility_protection = float(parameters["credibility_protection"])
    active_tie_ceiling = float(parameters["active_tie_ceiling"])
    tie_activation_rate = float(parameters["tie_activation_rate"])
    conflict_tie_boost = float(parameters["conflict_tie_boost"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    lapse = float(parameters["lapse"])
    competition_type = int(parameters["competition_type"])

    # Six correlated mixture cells preserve the previous marginal distribution
    # of active-tie accessibility while assigning only one-sixth of subjects to
    # a genuinely singleton-resistant group. The remaining subjects express a
    # strong but heterogeneous exact-singleton challenge response.
    if competition_type == 0:       # genuinely singleton-resistant
        type_challenge = 0.05
        type_singleton_access = 0.00
    elif competition_type in (1, 2):  # strongly challenge-sensitive
        type_challenge = 4.50
        type_singleton_access = 0.00
    else:                            # strongly accessible integrators
        type_challenge = 1.00
        type_singleton_access = 1.50

    # Tie accessibility is crossed with singleton sensitivity so that changing
    # the singleton mixture does not change the marginal tie-type frequencies.
    if competition_type in (0, 1):
        type_tie = 1.65
    elif competition_type in (2, 3):
        type_tie = 0.30
    else:
        type_tie = 1.00

    def sigmoid(x):
        x = float(np.clip(x, -60.0, 60.0))
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-x))

    # Communicated accuracy is represented on a log-evidence scale. Centering
    # on the active maximum improves numerical stability without discarding
    # absolute validity, which is retained separately below.
    v = np.clip(validities, 0.500001, 0.999999)
    reliability = np.log(v / (1.0 - v))
    active_reference = float(np.max(reliability[active]))
    cue_weight = np.exp(validity_gain * (reliability - active_reference))

    a_cues = np.flatnonzero(directions < 0)
    b_cues = np.flatnonzero(directions > 0)
    n_a = int(a_cues.size)
    n_b = int(b_cues.size)

    def coalition_support(indices):
        n = int(indices.size)
        if n == 0:
            return 0.0

        weights = np.asarray(cue_weight[indices], dtype=float)
        raw_support = float(np.sum(weights))

        # Effective multiplicity changes smoothly with coalition composition.
        # A coalition containing several similarly accessible cues has a high
        # effective count and is compressed more strongly than a heterogeneous
        # coalition dominated by one cue.
        effective_n = raw_support / max(float(np.max(weights)), 1e-12)
        effective_excess = max(effective_n - 1.0, 0.0)

        coalition_v = validities[indices]
        validity_spread = float(np.std(coalition_v)) if n > 1 else 0.0
        similarity = np.exp(-similarity_sensitivity * validity_spread)
        discount = 1.0 + redundancy_strength * similarity * (
            effective_excess ** redundancy_curvature
        )
        return raw_support / max(discount, 1e-12)

    support_a = coalition_support(a_cues)
    support_b = coalition_support(b_cues)

    # The validity anchor is defined only over currently discriminating cues.
    active_v = validities[active]
    best_v = float(np.max(active_v))
    top_candidates = active[np.isclose(active_v, best_v, atol=1e-8)]
    anchor_cue = int(np.min(top_candidates))
    anchor_direction = float(directions[anchor_cue])
    unique_anchor = float(top_candidates.size == 1)

    # In unique-anchor multi-cue-versus-multi-cue configurations, normalize
    # coalition composition toward effective count support. This saturation
    # prevents reallocating one relatively valid lower cue from inducing an
    # implicit primacy crossover, while leaving isolated-anchor diagnostics
    # and all tied-top configurations unchanged.
    normalized_multicue_geometry = False
    if unique_anchor > 0.0 and n_a > 1 and n_b > 1:
        pooled_weight = float(np.mean(cue_weight[active]))

        def normalized_multicue_support(n):
            excess = float(n - 1)
            discount = 1.0 + redundancy_strength * (
                excess ** redundancy_curvature
            )
            return pooled_weight * float(n) / max(discount, 1e-12)

        support_a = normalized_multicue_support(n_a)
        support_b = normalized_multicue_support(n_b)
        normalized_multicue_geometry = True

    if anchor_direction > 0:
        anchor_indices = b_cues
        opponent_indices = a_cues
        anchor_support = support_b
        opponent_support = support_a
    else:
        anchor_indices = a_cues
        opponent_indices = b_cues
        anchor_support = support_a
        opponent_support = support_b

    anchor_count = int(anchor_indices.size)
    opponent_count = int(opponent_indices.size)

    # Absolute credibility and relative advantage are distinct. A cue can be
    # locally strongest yet remain challengeable when all active cues have low
    # communicated validity.
    weak_anchor = sigmoid(absolute_slope * (absolute_threshold - best_v))
    strong_anchor = 1.0 - weak_anchor

    if opponent_count > 0:
        strongest_opponent_v = float(np.max(validities[opponent_indices]))
        opponent_gap = max(best_v - strongest_opponent_v, 0.0)
    else:
        opponent_gap = 0.5

    gap_accessibility = np.exp(
        -opponent_gap / max(challenge_gap_scale, 1e-8)
    )
    gap_protection = 1.0 - gap_accessibility

    # Credibility protection is deliberately bounded so that merely moving a
    # relatively valid lower cue between coalitions cannot create an implicit
    # unique-anchor presentation-order effect.
    anchor_support *= 1.0 + (
        unique_anchor
        * credibility_protection
        * strong_anchor
        * gap_protection
    )

    if opponent_count > 0:
        # The high-amplitude component is extremely localized at one opponent.
        # Embedded singleton dissent receives only a bounded fraction of it,
        # whereas isolated one-versus-one conflict expresses the full stable
        # subject-type difference. In that exact geometry, a bounded access
        # increment selectively raises strongly accessible integrators while a
        # small mixture remains genuinely resistant.
        count_distance = (
            float(opponent_count) - compact_peak
        ) / max(compact_width, 1e-8)
        singleton_profile = np.exp(-0.5 * count_distance ** 2)

        if anchor_count == 1:
            singleton_geometry = 1.0
        else:
            singleton_geometry = embedded_compact_scale

        active_type_challenge = type_challenge
        if (
            unique_anchor > 0.0
            and anchor_count == 1
            and opponent_count == 1
            and top_candidates.size == 1
        ):
            active_type_challenge += (
                isolated_singleton_access * type_singleton_access
            )

        singleton_intensity = (
            active_type_challenge
            * compact_challenge
            * singleton_profile
            * singleton_geometry
        )
        smooth_tail = challenge_tail / float(opponent_count + 1)

        isolation = 1.0 / float(max(anchor_count, 1))
        geometry_gain = 1.0 + isolation_gain * isolation
        absolute_gain = 1.0 + weak_anchor_gain * weak_anchor

        challenge_multiplier = 1.0 + (
            singleton_intensity + smooth_tail
        ) * gap_accessibility * geometry_gain * absolute_gain
        opponent_support *= challenge_multiplier

    total_support = anchor_support + opponent_support
    if total_support <= 1e-12:
        core_evidence = 0.0
    else:
        anchor_margin = (anchor_support - opponent_support) / total_support
        core_evidence = anchor_direction * anchor_margin

    # A bounded order gate is activated exclusively by a tie among currently
    # active maximum-validity cues. Conflict among tied maxima receives an
    # additional activation increment only when lower-validity active cues
    # precede the tied set. This captures activation-sensitive accessibility
    # without increasing first-cue adherence in unique-maximum profiles.
    active_top_count = int(top_candidates.size)
    if active_top_count >= 2:
        tie_gate = (
            type_tie
            * active_tie_ceiling
            * (1.0 - np.exp(
                -tie_activation_rate * float(active_top_count - 1)
            ))
        )
        tied_directions = directions[top_candidates]
        tied_conflict = float(
            np.any(tied_directions > 0) and np.any(tied_directions < 0)
        )
        preceded_tied_set = float(int(active[0]) < anchor_cue)
        tie_gate += (
            type_tie
            * conflict_tie_boost
            * tied_conflict
            * preceded_tied_set
        )
    else:
        tie_gate = 0.0
    tie_gate = float(np.clip(tie_gate, 0.0, 0.95))

    choice_evidence = (
        (1.0 - tie_gate) * core_evidence
        + tie_gate * anchor_direction
    )

    # Symmetric multi-cue normalization removes much of the identity-based
    # conflict, so choices in that geometry are moderately more precise. This
    # affects neither isolated singleton competition nor active-top-tie trials.
    effective_beta = beta * (1.60 if normalized_multicue_geometry else 1.0)
    logits = effective_beta * np.array(
        [-0.5 * choice_evidence, 0.5 * choice_evidence],
        dtype=np.float64,
    )
    logits = logits - np.max(logits)
    probs = np.exp(logits)
    probs /= probs.sum()

    probs = (1.0 - lapse) * probs + lapse * np.array(
        [0.5, 0.5], dtype=np.float64
    )
    probs = np.clip(probs, 0.0, None)
    total = float(probs.sum())
    if not np.isfinite(total) or total <= 0.0:
        return np.array([0.5, 0.5], dtype=np.float64)
    probs /= total
    return probs.astype(np.float64)

experiment.rationale: This design isolates ADCG's reliability-sensitive learning of anti-concurrence from discrimination-frequency rarity. Expert 1 is the unique 95%-valid anchor. Experts 2 and 5 have identical 74% validity and discriminate equally often across the block, but Expert 5 is deliberately presented later. The two critical targets are otherwise matched one-versus-one conflicts: Expert 1 supports the anchor option while either Expert 5 (diagnostic target) or Expert 2 (control target) supports the other option. ACAC assigns these targets exactly the same evidence: both have the same unique anchor, opponent validity, validity gap, absolute credibility, coalition counts, and singleton-challenge geometry. Because the maximum validity is unique, ACAC does not use presentation order, and because it excludes history learning, it predicts an exactly zero diagnostic-minus-control target contrast at every experience level. The history-building trials equate Experts 2 and 5 in marginal discrimination frequency. Expert 5, however, repeatedly opposes Expert 1 whenever they discriminate together, providing many observations of their perfectly anti-concurrent relationship. Expert 2 also opposes Expert 1 on its target, but its five builders occur while Expert 1 is nondiscriminating; hence its relationship with the anchor remains much less well observed. This distinguishes confidence in a learned relationship from merely estimating a high opposition proportion. ADCG initially favors the control dissenter because Expert 2 appears much earlier than the equally valid Expert 5. With experience, the well-observed Expert-1/Expert-5 opposition crosses ADCG's reliability-sensitive anti-concurrence gate more strongly, amplifies Expert 5's dissent, suppresses the anchor-protecting profile gate, and attenuates the unique early anchor. Thus ADCG predicts that [P(anchor choice | diagnostic target) - P(anchor choice | control target)] decreases with cumulative experience and may reverse sign, whereas ACAC predicts this contrast and its experience interaction to be exactly zero. Diagnostic and control builders both contain three active cues, while varied shared ratings create distinct displays without changing directional evidence. Every profile has an exact A/B reversal. The 24 unique pairs are repeated four times, yielding 96 trials.

metric.rationale: This is a reversal-invariant difference-in-differences for the critical targets. A response is coded as choosing the option supported by the unique 0.95-valid anchor (Expert 1). Within each subject, it measures the late-minus-early change in anchor choice for Expert-1-versus-Expert-5 diagnostic conflicts, then subtracts the corresponding change for matched Expert-1-versus-Expert-2 control conflicts. Early and late are defined by condition-specific occurrence rank, guaranteeing balanced observations despite randomized trial order. ACAC is history-independent and gives the two equally valid dissenters matched target evidence, so its expected interaction is zero. ADCG predicts a negative interaction because repeated, reliable Expert-1/Expert-5 anti-concurrence increasingly strengthens Expert 5 and attenuates the anchor, whereas the Expert-1/Expert-2 relationship remains less well learned. Subtracting the matched control change also removes generic drift, anchor preference, and much stable subject heterogeneity.

proposer_theory.description: Adaptive Distinctive Coalition Gating (ADCG) proposes that binary-feature decisions arise from task-adaptive cue weights combining communicated validity, presentation prominence, distributional rarity, and learned cue dependence. Directionally concordant cues are compressed as potentially redundant, while sparse dissent can dominate when its cues have reliably and repeatedly opposed the anchor's cues. Learned anti-concurrence is reliability-sensitive: disagreement near chance is strongly suppressed, whereas well-observed disagreement above a subject-specific threshold receives a bounded nonlinear gain. A profile-driven gate interpolates between coalition comparison and a lexicographic anchor, preserving anchoring against large redundant coalitions while permitting diagnostic opposition to suppress it. For compact opposition, gate suppression is controlled by a selective summary of the strongest reliably learned opposing relationship rather than an indiscriminate average across all cue pairs; larger coalitions retain mean aggregation and strong size decay. In addition, a unique, early-presented validity anchor loses accessibility within the coalition core when it faces compact, reliably anti-concurrent opposition. This attenuation targets residual anchoring without increasing dissent support and vanishes for tied-validity anchors, late anchors, and large opposing coalitions. When top validities are tied, presentation order supplies a bounded anchor but the distinctive-coalition core is attenuated by a stable subject-specific amount. Stable variation in validity attention, order prominence, anti-concurrence threshold and gain, diagnostic selectivity, anchor attenuation, tied-top attenuation, redundancy, gating, and temperature produces structured individual differences without experiment-specific strategies.
